cues: The metre is the common metre of the hymn book, the metre of Amazing Grace: lines of eight and six syllables, iambic tetrameter and trimeter.
But count: in the first three stanzas the opening line is one syllable short.
It is headless, starting on a stress, a little push forward.
Only the last stanza fills out to perfect hymn metre, exactly as the poem becomes religious.
text: The metre is the common metre of the hymn book, the metre of Amazing Grace: lines of eight and six syllables, iambic tetrameter and trimeter. Dickinson sang it every Sunday. But count: in the first three stanzas the opening line is one syllable short. It is headless, starting on a stress, a little push forward. Only the last stanza fills out to perfect hymn metre, exactly as the poem becomes religious. That is not an accident.
